BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.claim: The source notes two verses beginning يا أيها الإنسان, one asking what deceived the person about the generous Lord and one saying the person labors toward the Lord.
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r12.anchor: وفيه ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم ﴾ ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان إنك كادح ﴾

ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.claim: Asad reports that some authorities date the surah to early Mecca, while others consider it more likely to belong to the last group of Meccan revelations.
ASAD-NOTES:82:intro/r1.anchor: others regard it as more probable that it belongs to the last group of Meccan revelations

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.claim: Al-Infiṭār is the counterpart of al-Takwīr, sharing its intrinsic and extrinsic form, style, meanings, and opening cataclysm.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r1.anchor: great similarity between the intrinsic and extrinsic form, style and meanings of both sūrahs.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.claim: Both sūrahs address rich, arrogant Quraysh who ignored the warnings because they trusted their castles and edifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r4.anchor: The real addressees of both sūrahs are the rich and arrogant among the Quraysh who were turning a deaf ear to the warnings of the Qur’ ān just because they thought that no one would be able to break into their castles and edifices.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.claim: Al-Takwīr reasons from the Qur’an’s authenticity, source, revelation, and bearer; its rejecters cannot distinguish radiant dawn from murky night.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r5.anchor: the bearer are all pure and upright.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p212/r6.claim: Al-Infiṭār instead reasons from God’s creativity, power, wisdom, justice, and mercy: signs of power and mercy in humans entail a coming day of reward and punishment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.claim: Resurrection is no difficulty for God: if first creation was easy, creating again is no harder, and the coming day is certain.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r1.anchor: creating again be difficult for Him?

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r2.claim: God’s present respite for criminals gives them time to reform; those who refuse have no excuse or justification at Judgment.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.claim: Divine delay does not mean words and deeds are hidden: angels have been assigned to everyone to record everything.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r3.anchor: This delay from God should not mislead people to think that their words or deeds are hidden from Him. He has deputed His angels on every person who are noting down each and everything.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.claim: Human formation displays divine power, wisdom, mercy, and justice, showing that Judgment is possible and that human existence has purpose.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p213/r5.anchor: With reference to the grandeur of divine attributes of power, wisdom, mercy and justice found in the formation of a human being a reminder is sounded that no one should think that the Day of Judgement is beyond the power of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r3.claim: God’s continued respite is benevolence, but the disbelievers mistake it for grounds to feel safe; they should be grateful, yet mock the warnings and presume their wealth is their birthright.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p218/r3.anchor: The Almighty does not seize them immediately on their misdeeds and continues to give them respite.

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r7.claim: The question asks what deceived or misled a person into disobeying God.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r7.anchor: أي : ما خدعك وما سول لك حتى عملت بمعاصيه

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r8.claim: One prompted answer is that God's generosity emboldened the sinner: He saw and concealed, and could punish but granted respite.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r8.anchor: غرني كرمك بي ، ولولا كرمك لما فعلت ؛ لأنك رأيت فسترت ، وقدرت فأمهلت

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r9.claim: Another interpretation says a believer trusts God's beneficence and is deceived by prolonged respite; forbearance emboldens bad conduct despite the believer's presumption that a lapse was impossible.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r9.anchor: إن المؤمن وثق بحسن إفضاله فاغتر بطول إمهاله فلم يرتكب الزلة لاستحاله ، ولكن طول حلمه عنه حمله على سوء خصاله

QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r10.claim: Qushayri's couplet dramatizes the sinner's excuse: God's repeated generosity has emboldened him despite the Master's rebuke.
QUSHAYRI:v3p399/r10.anchor: يقول مولاي : أما تستحي . . . مما أرى من سوء أفعالك قلت : يا مولاي رفقا فقد . . . جرأني كثرة أفضالك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r8.claim: ‘What deluded you’ means what made a person see a bad deed as good or presume certain forgiveness; the famous reading also conveys astonishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r8.anchor: { ما غرك } أي أدخلك في الغرة , وهي أن ترى فعلك القبيح حسنا أو ترى أنه يعفى عنك لا محالة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والأعمش
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r9.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read with an interrogative hamza, ‘Did He delude you?’, while the well-known reading adds a sense of astonishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r9.anchor: وذلك بمعنى قراءة سعيد بن جبير والأعمش : أغرك بهمزة الإنكار , وتزيد المشهورة معنى التعجب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r10.claim: Calling God ‘your Lord’ recalls His care and beneficence, which should not make people forget that they were created to save themselves by following His law.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r10.anchor: { بربك } أي المحسن إليك الذي أنساك إحسانه ما خلقت له من خلاص نفسك بعمل ما شرعه لك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r11.claim: God’s generosity entails that He does not neglect the unjust or equate obedient and disobedient people; it should prompt gratitude, obedience, and fear of His power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r11.anchor: المقتضي لئلا يهمل الظالم بل يمهله , ولا يسوي بين المحسن والمسيء والموالي والمعادي والمطيع والعاصي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r12.claim: The noble, generous one may be forbearing yet formidable when offended, whereas a base person lacks the means to punish; this sharpens the rebuke for presuming on divine generosity.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r12.anchor: فإنه يكون شديد الحلم عظيم السطوة عند انتهاك حرمته بعد ذلك الحلم فإنه يجد أعوانا كثيرة على مراده

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r13.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r13.claim: Al-Warrāq says he would answer that the generosity and forbearance of the Generous One deluded him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r13.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : لو سألني لقلبت : غرني كرم الكريم وحلمه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r14.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r14.claim: ʿAlī says a man’s servants’ poor manners reflect the man’s own poor discipline.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r14.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه : من كرم الرجل سوء أدب غلمانه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r15.speaker: الإمام الغزالي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r15.claim: Al-Ghazālī defines the Generous as one who pardons when able, fulfills promises, gives beyond measure, refuses another’s rejection of a petitioner, admonishes without exacting all due, protects those seeking refuge, and dispenses with intermediaries.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p348#s082/r15.anchor: وقال الإمام الغزالي في شرحه للأسماء : هو الذي إذا قدر عفا , وإذا وعد وفى , وإذا أعطى زاد على منتهى الرجال

STUDYQURAN:82:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:82:intro/r4.claim: Verses 6–12 reproach and warn people about the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:82:intro/r4.anchor: This is followed by a reproach and warning of the Last Day (vv. 6–12).

TABATABAI:82:19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:19/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:82:19/r1.claim: A report reaching Salih ibn Mismar says the Prophet recited the question about what deluded a person regarding his generous Lord, then answered that it was ignorance.
TABATABAI:82:19/r1.anchor: عن صالح بن مسمار قال بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم تلا هذه الآية

TABRISI:82:19/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:19/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:82:19/r7.claim: In a noncanonical reading Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads ma agharraka bi-rabbika, which may ask what caused the person to be deceived or express astonishment.
TABRISI:82:19/r7.anchor: وفي الشواذ قراءة سعيد بن جبير ما أغرك بربك.

TABRISI:82:19/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:19/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:19/r8.claim: The expression can also be understood as an exclamation, as can the wording in the cited verse about people being patient over the Fire.
TABRISI:82:19/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تعجبا وقد قيل في قوله

TABRISI:82:19/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:19/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:19/r9.claim: A lexical derivation from ghirr or gharara yields the sense how ignorant or heedless you are; deriving it from ghurur is also possible but irregular, as in the cited idiom.
TABRISI:82:19/r9.anchor: وأغرك يجوز أن يكون من الغر والغرارة فيكون معناه ما أجهلك وما أغفلك عما يراد بك

TABRISI:82:1-19/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19/r1.speaker: الحرث بن حلزة
TABRISI:82:1-19/r1.claim: Al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line says they did not deceive you, illustrating the word gharur.
TABRISI:82:1-19/r1.anchor: لم يغروكم غرورا ولكن رفع الآل جمعهم والضحاء

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r1.claim: When the Prophet recited the question about what deludes a person from his Lord, he answered that ignorance had deluded him.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r1.anchor:
النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما تلا هذه الآية قال:
" غره جهله "

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r3.claim: The verse asks what deceived a person about his Creator and made him follow falsehood and disobey.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r3.anchor: أي أي شيء غرك بخالقك وخدعك وسول لك الباطل حتى عصيته وخالفته

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r4.claim: Al-Karim may mean the benefactor whose actions are pure generosity, with no pursuit of gain or defense against harm.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r4.anchor: هو المنعم الذي كل أفعاله إحسان وإنعام لا يجر به نفعا ولا يدفع به ضررا

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r5.claim: Another definition of al-Karim is one who gives what is due and beyond what is due without demanding what is owed to him.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r5.anchor: هو الذي يعطي من عليه وما ليس عليه ولا يطلب ماله

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r6.claim: Another definition says the Generous accepts a little and gives much.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r6.anchor: هو الذي يقبل اليسير ويعطي الكثير

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r7.claim: A further sign of God's generosity is that He does more than forgive sins: He changes them into good deeds.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r7.anchor: من كرمه سبحانه أنه لم يرض بالعفو عن السيئات حتى بدلها بالحسنات

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r8.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r8.claim: Asked what he would answer God, Fudayl says he would say that God's lowered veils had deceived him.

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r9.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh says he would answer that God's past and present kindness had deceived him.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r9.anchor: قلت غرني بك برك بي سالفا وآنفا

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r10.claim: Other answers say that God's forbearance or the generosity of the Generous was what deceived the speaker.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r10.anchor: وعن بعضهم قال غرني حلمك وعن أبي بكر الوراق غرني كرم الكريم

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r11.claim: The verse names God al-Karim rather than another attribute as if prompting the reply that the Generous One's generosity was what deceived the person.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r11.anchor: وإنما قال سبحانه الكريم دون سائر أسمائه وصفاته لأنه كأنه لقنه الإجابة

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r12.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says everyone will meet God alone on Resurrection Day and be asked what deceived him and what he did and answered the messengers.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r12.anchor: ما منكم من أحد إلا سيخلو الله به يوم القيامة فيقول يا بن آدم ما غرك بي

TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r13.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r13.claim: Ali warns that many are deluded by God's concealment of their faults and gradually drawn in by His favors.
TABRISI:82:1-19#2/r13.anchor: كم مغرور بالستر عليه ومستدرج بالإحسان إليه

STUDYQURAN:82:6/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:82:6/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:82:6/r1.claim: The two deluders are worldly life and Satan, called the Deluder.
STUDYQURAN:82:6/r1.anchor: Two things are said to delude human beings, the life of this world and Satan, the Deluder

TAB-FULL:v24p177/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p177/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p177/r1.claim: He addresses the disbelieving human and asks what deluded him about his generous Lord; the deluder is the enemy Satan empowered over him.
TAB-FULL:v24p177/r1.anchor: يا أيها الإنسان الكافر، أي شيء غرك بربك الكريم، غر الإنسان به عدوه المسلط عليه

TAB-FULL:v24p177/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p177/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p177/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the enemy that deluded Adam's son as Satan.
TAB-FULL:v24p177/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، {ما غرك بربك الكريم} [الانفطار: 6] شيء ما غر ابن آدم هذا العدو الشيطان

TABATABAI:82:6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:82:6/r4.claim: The addressee is the human who denies Judgment Day, as the surrounding passage indicates; denial of judgment entails denial of religious law and of God's lordship.
TABATABAI:82:6/r4.anchor: والمراد بهذا الانسان المكذب ليوم الدين

TABATABAI:82:6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:82:6/r5.claim: Addressing him as a human makes his human qualities collectively serve as proof against his ingratitude.
TABATABAI:82:6/r5.anchor: وإنما وجه الخطاب إليه بما أنه إنسان ليكون حجة أو كالحجة

TABATABAI:82:6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:82:6/r6.claim: Linking the rebuke to God's lordship and generosity makes the question an argument: rebellion against a managing Lord who pours out blessings is plainly ugly and deserves punishment.
TABATABAI:82:6/r6.anchor: وقد علق الغرور بصفتي ربوبيته وكرمه تعالى ليكون ذلك حجة في توجه العتاب والتوبيخ فإن تمرد المربوب

TABATABAI:82:6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:82:6/r7.claim: Ingratitude is especially blameworthy because the generous Lord seeks no benefit or repayment, tolerates wrongdoing, and forgives sins committed in ignorance.
TABATABAI:82:6/r7.anchor: وخاصة إذا كان الرب المنعم كريما لا يريد في نعمه وعطاياه نفعا ينتفع به ولا عضوا يقابله به المنعم عليه

TABATABAI:82:6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:82:6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:82:6/r8.claim: The question is a rebuke for a specific inexcusable ingratitude: failing to thank a generous Lord for His blessings.
TABATABAI:82:6/r8.anchor: استفهام توبيخي يوبخ الإنسان بكفران خاص لا عذر له يعتذر به عنه

BURSEVI:v10p276/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r5.claim: The address covers all disobedient people, not only unbelievers, since it falls between the general statement about every soul and its elaboration concerning the righteous.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r5.anchor: يا اأيها الانسان} يعم جميع العصاة ولا خصوص له بالكفار

BURSEVI:v10p276/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r6.claim: The later plural accusation that they deny the judgment can use a singular generic human, just as one person in a clan's action may be attributed to the clan.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r6.anchor: وأما قوله بل تكذبون بالدين فمن قبيل بنوا فلان

BURSEVI:v10p276/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r7.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p276/r7.claim: Al-Suhaylī says the intended person is Umayya ibn Khalaf, while the general wording also applies to others; other reports name al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra or al-Aswad ibn Kalada.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r7.anchor: قال الامام السهيلي رحمه الله قوله : يا أيها الإنسان يريد أمية بن خلف

BURSEVI:v10p276/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r8.claim: A report in Zahrat al-Riyāḍ says a man struck the Prophet on the crown, was thrown down by him, then asked for safety and promised not to harm him; the Prophet released him.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r8.anchor: وفي زهرة الرياض ضرب على يافوخ رسول الله عليه السلام ، فأخذه رسول الله

BURSEVI:v10p276/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r9.claim: The reproachful question asks what deceived and emboldened a person to disobey God and feel safe from punishment despite the calamities and deeds awaiting him.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r9.anchor: والاستفهام بمعنى الاستهجان والتوبيخ والمعنى أي شيء خدعك وجرأك على عصيانه

BURSEVI:v10p276/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r10.claim: To deceive someone regarding another is to embolden him and make him feel safe from danger on that person's account, though the danger is real.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r10.anchor: يقال غره بفلان إذا جرأه عليه وأمنه المحذور من جهته مع إنه غير مأمون

BURSEVI:v10p276/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r11.claim: Calling God generous does not justify complacency, despite Satan's suggestion that one may sin because God is generous; divine generosity should instead increase faith, obedience, and avoidance of sin.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r11.anchor: والتعرض لعنوان كرمه تعالى للإيذان بأنه ليس مما يصلح أن يكون مدار الاغترار

BURSEVI:v10p276/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v10p276/r12.claim: When the Prophet recited this verse, he said that ignorance had deceived the person.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r12.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قرأها غره جهله

BURSEVI:v10p276/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r13.speaker: الحسن البصري
BURSEVI:v10p276/r13.claim: Al-Hasan al-Baṣrī says that, by God, Satan deceived him.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r13.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري رحمه الله غره والله شيطنه

BURSEVI:v10p276/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p276/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p276/r14.claim: God's generosity calls for fear of disobedience: neglecting an oppressor would wrong the oppressed, and generosity cannot mean treating the hostile and devoted alike; paired divine names include mercy and painful punishment.
BURSEVI:v10p276/r14.anchor: من حيث إن إهمال الظالم ينافي كونه كريما بالنسبة إلى المظلوم

THALABI:v10p146/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r1.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v10p146/r1.claim: An admonitory couplet asks the sinner how he is unashamed when God is with him in private and says divine reprieve and concealment deceive him.
THALABI:v10p146/r1.anchor: يا كاتم الذنب أما تستحي … الله في الخلوة ثانيكا

THALABI:v10p146/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r2.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v10p146/r2.claim: Muqatil says God’s pardon deceives the sinner because punishment has not been hastened.
THALABI:v10p146/r2.anchor: وقال: مقاتل: غره عفو الله حين لم يعجل عليه بالعقوبة

THALABI:v10p146/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r3.speaker: نصر بن مغلس
THALABI:v10p146/r3.claim: Nasr ibn Maghlis says the sinner is deceived by God’s gentleness toward him.
THALABI:v10p146/r3.anchor: وتلا [نصر] بن مغلس هذه الآية فقال: غره رفق الله به.

THALABI:v10p146/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r4.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
THALABI:v10p146/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh imagines answering that God’s prior and continuing kindness is what deceived him.
THALABI:v10p146/r4.anchor: سمعت علي بن محمد الوراق يقول: سمعت يحيى بن معاذ يقول: لو أقامني الله سبحانه بين يديه

THALABI:v10p146/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r5.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v10p146/r5.claim: One answer to God’s question is that His forbearance deceived the sinner.
THALABI:v10p146/r5.anchor: سمعت حماد بن بكر يحكي عن بعضهم أنه قال: لو سألني عن هذا ربي لقلت: غرني حلمك

THALABI:v10p146/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r6.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v10p146/r6.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq answers that the Generous One’s generosity deceived him.
THALABI:v10p146/r6.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر الوراق يقول: لو قال لي ما غرك بربك الكريم لقلت: غرني كرم الكريم.

THALABI:v10p146/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r7.speaker: أهل الإشارة
THALABI:v10p146/r7.claim: The people of mystical allusion say the wording “your Lord, the Generous” cues the answer that the Generous One’s generosity was the cause.
THALABI:v10p146/r7.anchor: قال أهل الإشارة: إنما قال: بربك الكريم دون سائر أسمائه وصفاته

THALABI:v10p146/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r8.speaker: منصور بن عمار
THALABI:v10p146/r8.claim: Mansur ibn Ammar says only his knowledge of God’s grace toward servants and His pardoning them could have deceived him.
THALABI:v10p146/r8.anchor: قال منصور بن عمار لو قيل: ما غرك بي؟ قلت: يا رب ما غرني إلا ما علمته

THALABI:v10p146/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p146/r9.claim: Ibn Masud reports that God will privately ask every person at resurrection what deceived him, what he did with his knowledge, and how he answered the messengers.
THALABI:v10p146/r9.anchor: وروى أبو وائل عن ابن مسعود قال: ما منكم من أحد إلا سيخلو الله سبحانه وتعالى به يوم القيامة

THALABI:v10p146/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r10.speaker: ذو النون المصري
THALABI:v10p146/r10.claim: Dhu al-Nun warns that many are deluded while protected under the veil without realizing it.
THALABI:v10p146/r10.anchor: سمعت يوسف بن الحسين يقول: سمعت ذا النون المصري يقول: كم من مغرور تحت الستر وهو لا يشعر.

THALABI:v10p146/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p146/r11.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر الأبهري
THALABI:v10p146/r11.claim: A verse recited by Abu Bakr ibn Tahir warns that wealth, pride, and prolonged reprieve let a sinner confront God without fearing the consequences.
THALABI:v10p146/r11.anchor: أنشدنا أبو بكر بن طاهر الأبهري في هذا المعنى: يا من غلا في الغنى والتيه … وغره طول تماديه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r1.claim: The address is directed to the disbelievers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r2.claim: The question asks what deceived the human and enticed him into falsehood until he neglected what was due to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r2.anchor: (أي ما خدعك، وسول إليك الباطل حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r3.claim: It also asks who made him feel safe from punishment; the idiom means giving someone false assurance against a danger from an unreliable source, as in 35:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r3.anchor: والمعنى: ما الذي أمنك من عقابه، ويقال: غره بفلان، إذا أمنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r4.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r4.anchor: قال (عطاء عن) (¬1) ابن عباس: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r5.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says it was revealed about Abu al-Ashaddayn Kalda ibn Asid, who struck the Prophet but was not punished, prompting the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r5.anchor: وقال الكلبي: نزلت في أبي الأشدين كلدة بن أسيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r6.claim: Qatada says the enemy set over the human, Satan, deceived him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r6.anchor: فقال قتادة: غره العدو المسلط عليه، يعني الشيطان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r7.speaker: الربيع بن خثيم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Khuthaym says ignorance deceived him; the report is transmitted as raised to the Prophet.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r8.claim: Muqatil says God’s forbearance deceived him, since He did not punish him immediately.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p292#2/r8.anchor: وقال مقاتل: غره عفو الله عنه حين لم يعاقبه في أول أمره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r6.claim: The question asks what deceived a person into adorning falsehood and neglecting what God required.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:82:1-7/r6.anchor: { يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم } أي: ما خدعك وسول لك الباطل حتى أضعت ما أوجب عليك.

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r1.claim: After announcing the Resurrection, the passage prompts rational reflection as a reminder and warning.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r1.anchor: Bu suretle haşr u neşrin vukū‘u haber verildikten sonra aklen de onu düşündürmesi lâzım gelen bir tezkir ve ihtar

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r2.speaker: Atâ
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r2.claim: Atā reports that the verse was revealed concerning Walid b. Mughirah.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r2.anchor: Atâ’dan, bu âyetin Velîd b. Mugīre sebebiyle

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r3.speaker: İkrime
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r3.claim: Ikrimah reports that the verse was revealed concerning Ubayy b. Khalaf.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r3.anchor: İkrime’den Übey b. Halef sebebiyle nâzil olduğu

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r4.speaker: Kelbî ve Mukātil
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil report that the verse was revealed concerning Asad b. Kelede.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r4.anchor: Kelbî ve Mukātil’den de Esed b. Kelede sebebiyle

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r5.claim: A report says the offender struck the Prophet; God did not punish him immediately but revealed this verse.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r5.anchor: Hazret-i Peygamber’e vurmuştu. Allah teâlâ hemen ona ukūbet buyurmayıp bu âyeti inzal eyledi

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r6.speaker: birçokları
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r6.claim: Many commentators take “the human” here to mean a disbelieving human, in light of the following denial of the Judgment.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r6.anchor: birçokları burada “insan”dan murad kâfir insan demek olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r7.claim: Author favors the word’s general scope: all people who rebel through delusion are included, since a specific occasion does not restrict a general ruling.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r7.anchor: sebebin hususiyeti hükmün umumiyetine mâni‘olmayacağı cihetle diğer birçokları da gurur ile isyan eden insanların hepsine şâmil olması lafzın umûmuna daha muvâfık

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r8.claim: The question asks what made the person arrogant, deceived, and led him into disobedience and unworthy conduct.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r8.anchor: seni ne mağrur etti ne şey aldattı, iğfal etti de isyâna sevketti

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r9.claim: Although this is a warning, invoking the Lord as Generous rather than emphasizing punitive attributes conveys a subtle moral lesson about divine generosity.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r9.anchor: Bu hitab ve sual inzar hitâbı olmak hasebiyle gurûra mâni‘olacak kahr u celâl sıfatlarından biri zikrolunmak zâhir görünürken, “Kerîm” vasfıyla bilhassa kerem-i ilâhînin ihtar olunmasında ince bir nükte

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r10.claim: The Lord’s generosity calls for greater faith, gratitude, obedience, respect, and moral elevation, with avoidance of ingratitude and rebellion.

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r11.claim: Treating generosity as leave to sin—“God is generous, so do as you wish”—is a false analogy; generosity is joined with wisdom, and generosity used without wisdom would be wastefulness.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r11.anchor: Şeytanların dediği gibi “adam sen de, Allah Kerîm’dir, istediğini yap, dünyada sana ettiği fazl u keremini âhirette de eder” diyerek lâubâlîlik etmek, yanlış bir kıyas ile aldanmaktır

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r12.claim: He identifies this warning against being deceived about God with the teaching of Fatir 35:5.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r12.anchor: ihtar edilmiştir ki bu mâna tamamen

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r13.claim: Author rejects the widespread reading that the question prompts the answer “Your generosity deluded me,” because it conflicts with the surah’s warning tone.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r13.anchor: Bu suâli bazıları “beni keremin mağrur etti yâ Rab!” dedirtmek için

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r14.claim: A believer who sins despite knowing God’s generosity feels shame and remorse at this address, a response unbelievers cannot feel in the same way.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r14.anchor: kerem-i ilâhîye imanı olduğu hâlde âsî olmuş bir mü’minin bu hitabdan duyacağı hicab ve teessür, kâfirlerin duyamayacağı bir hiss-i teessür

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r15.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r15.claim: A Prophetic hadith calls Suhayb an excellent servant who would not disobey God even if he did not fear Him.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r15.anchor: نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ صُهَيْب لَوْ لَمْ يَخَفِ اللهَ لَمْ يـَعْصِهِ “Suheyb ne güzel kuldur, Allah’tan korkmasa idi bile isyan etmezdi”

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r16.speaker: Bazı ârifînin
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r16.claim: Some spiritual knowers express the same reverence by saying that even without fear of God they could not disobey.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r16.anchor: Bazı ârifînin “Allah’tan korkmasa idim yine isyan edemezdim”

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r17.claim: Fatir 35:28 states that those servants who truly fear God are the learned; the author links reverential fear to knowledge of God.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r17.anchor: âyeti de bunu nâtık olduğu geçmişti

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r18.speaker: Katâde
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r18.claim: Qatadah identifies Satan’s embellishment as what deludes people; the author connects the report to Hadid 57:14.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r18.anchor: Katâde’den mervî olduğu üzere, Şeytan’ın tesvîlidir. وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلْغَرُورُ

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r19.speaker: Hasan
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r19.claim: Hasan identifies ignorance as what deludes people.

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r20.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r20.claim: Muqatil says people are deluded into expecting pardon because punishment was not imposed immediately.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r20.anchor: Mukātil’den rivayet edildiği üzere, evvelemirde ukūbet

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r21.speaker: Fuzayl b. İyaz
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r21.claim: Asked what he would answer on Judgment Day, Fudayl says he would answer: “Your lowered veils,” meaning God’s concealment of sins.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r21.anchor: Fuzayl b. İyaz Hazretleri’ne “kıyamet günü مَا غَرَّكَ بِرَبِّكَ ٱلْكَرِيمِ

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r22.claim: Trusting delayed punishment or divine concealment reduces to ignorance; being taken in by Satan’s embellishment does too.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r22.anchor: bu son ikisi, yani ikābda acele edilmediğinden dolayı affa ve setre güvenmek cehalete râci‘dir. Şeytan’ın tesvîlâtına aldanmak da öyle demektir

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r23.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r23.claim: Reports recorded by Abu Hayyan and Alusi say the Prophet recited this verse and answered, “Ignorance.”
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r23.anchor: Ebû Hayyân’ın ve Âlûsî’nin kaydettikleri vechile Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den rivayet olunmuştur ki bu âyeti kıraat etmiş de جهل demiştir

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r24.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r24.claim: Umar likewise answered “ignorance” and recited Ahzab 33:72.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r24.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer radıyallahu anh da bunu söyleyip

ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r25.claim: The interpretation as ignorance accords with the restriction in Fatir 35:28: fear of God grows in proportion to one’s knowledge of Him.
ELMALILI:82:1-7#2/r25.anchor: kasrına muvâfakati de âşikârdır. Demek ki haşyet Allah’a dair bilginin derecesiyle mütenâsibdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r1.claim: “O human” addresses especially those who deny the Resurrection, afterlife, and judgment, or consider them impossible, rather than one individual or all people indiscriminately.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r1.anchor: buradaki “ey insan” hitabıyla özellikle belli bir kişiye veya bütün insanlara değil, sûrenin asıl konusu olan kıyamet, âhiret ve uhrevî yargılanma ve hesap vermeyi inkâr edenlere

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r2.claim: Rabb and karīm name God’s graciousness toward His servants and belong to the divine attributes of beauty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:82:6/r2.anchor: Rab ismi ve bu ismin sıfatı olarak geçen kerîm, Cenâb-ı Hakk’ın “cemal sıfatları” denilen ve kullarına yönelik lütufkârlığını ifade eden isim ve sıfatlarındandır

BURHAN:v2p216/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p216/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p216/r2.claim: One mode of Quranic address is general address intended generally, illustrated by the call to humanity in 82:6.
BURHAN:v2p216/r2.anchor: الأول خطاب العام المراد به العموم

BURHAN:v4p403/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p403/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p403/r8.claim: The author classifies mā in the two Qur'anic exclamations as exclamatory; there is no third example except in Saʿīd ibn Jubayr's reading of 82:6.

BURHAN:v4p403/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p403/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BURHAN:v4p403/r9.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads mā in the question about what deceived the human as exclamatory.
BURHAN:v4p403/r9.anchor: إلا في قراءة سعيد بن جبير

BURHAN:v2p318/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r1.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p318/r1.claim: One view disallows marveling at God's act, since saying how great God is might suggest that something made Him great, whereas His attributes are eternal.
BURHAN:v2p318/r1.anchor: لايتعجب من فعل الله فلا يقال ما أعظم الله

BURHAN:v2p318/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p318/r2.claim: Another view permits such language because magnifying God accords with worshippers' belief in His greatness and power; an anonymous poem says He can bring the distant near.
BURHAN:v2p318/r2.anchor: وقيل بجوازه باعتبار انه يحب تعظيم الله شيء من صفاته

BURHAN:v2p318/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
BURHAN:v2p318/r3.claim: Some scholars answer that astonishment magnifies the matter itself; it need not imply that another agent caused it, and its cause may simply be hidden from us.
BURHAN:v2p318/r3.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين التعحب انما يقال لتعظيم الامر المتعجب منه

BURHAN:v2p318/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p318/r6.claim: The preferred view treats divine astonishment as directed toward the audience: God knows why people marvel, and His knowledge of what merits wonder is called wonder.
BURHAN:v2p318/r6.anchor: والمختار الاول وما وقع منه اول بالنظر إلى المخاطب أي علمت اسباب ما يتعجب منه العباد

BURHAN:v2p318/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p318/r7.claim: The dispute turns on whether true astonishment requires that the cause of the astonishing matter be hidden.
BURHAN:v2p318/r7.anchor: وأصل الخلاف في هذه المسالة يلتف على خلاف آخر وهو أن حقيقة التعجب

BURHAN:v2p318/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p318/r8.claim: The Qur'anic exclamation forms are limited to فما أصبرهم على النار, قتل الإنسان ما أكفره, and يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك in a reading that adds a hamza.
BURHAN:v2p318/r8.anchor: ولم يقع في القرآن صيغة التعجب الا

BURHAN:v2p318/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.speaker: المحققون
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.claim: The learned explain divine exclamation, prayer, and hope from the hearer's perspective; Sibawayh reads 20:44 as Moses and Aaron acting on their own hope, which Ibn al-Da'i praises.
BURHAN:v2p318/r9.anchor: ثم قال المحققون التعجب مصروف إلى المخاطب ولهذا تلطف الزمخشري

BURHAN:v2p337/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p337/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p337/r8.claim: Interrogatives can function as performative speech acts, including commands; for example, ‘will you not reflect?’ means ‘reflect.’
BURHAN:v2p337/r8.anchor: القسم الثاني الاستفهام المراد به الإنشاء وهو على ضروب الأول مجرد الطلب وهو الأمر

BURHAN:v2p337/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p337/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p337/r10.claim: The question ‘what has beguiled you by your generous Lord?’ functions as a prohibition: do not let anything beguile you.

ITQAN:v3p215/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p215/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p215/r2.claim: Interrogation can function as prohibition: ‘What deceived you by your generous Lord?’ means do not be deceived; other examples command fear of God rather than people.
ITQAN:v3p215/r2.anchor: السابع عشر النهي نحو ﴿ أتخشونهم فالله أحق أن تخشوه ﴾

ITQAN:v3p89/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p89/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p89/r7.claim: A singular address may address humanity collectively, as in “O human.”
ITQAN:v3p89/r7.anchor: الثالث عشر خطاب الجمع بلفظ الواحد نحو ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم ﴾

ITQAN:v2p512#4/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p512#4/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v2p512#4/r6.claim: In Saʿid ibn Jubayr’s recitation, “How deceived you are by your generous Lord” is a third exclamatory mā example.
ITQAN:v2p512#4/r6.anchor: إلا في قراءة سعيد بن جبير ما أغرك بربك الكريم ومحلها رفع بالابتداء وما بعدها خبر وهي نكرة تامة

TUSTARI:82:6/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r1.claim: What deludes a person is what cuts him off from God despite God's gentleness and generosity.
TUSTARI:82:6/r1.anchor: أي ما غرك بدونه فقطعك عنه مع لطفه وكرمه

TUSTARI:82:6/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r2.claim: Nothing is nearer to the servant than the believer's heart; when something other than God enters it, that presence becomes a veil.
TUSTARI:82:6/r2.anchor: وليس شيء أقرب إليه من قلب المؤمن، فإذا حضر الغير فيه فهو الحجاب

TUSTARI:82:6/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r3.claim: One who beholds God with the heart becomes distant from everything besides Him.
TUSTARI:82:6/r3.anchor: ومن نظر إلى الله بقلبه بعد عن كل شيء دونه

TUSTARI:82:6/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r4.claim: Whoever seeks God's good pleasure, He makes content through His forbearance.

TUSTARI:82:6/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r5.claim: When someone surrenders the heart to God, God takes charge of the limbs and makes them upright.
TUSTARI:82:6/r5.anchor: ومن أسلم إلى الله تعالى قلبه تولى جوارحه فاستقامت

TUSTARI:82:6/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r6.claim: The heart's testimony reflects the degree to which a person has guarded the limbs.
TUSTARI:82:6/r6.anchor: وإنما شهدت قلوبهم على قدر ما حفظوا من الجوارح

TUSTARI:82:6/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r7.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r7.claim: Keep the heart steadfast in awareness that the Creator is with His creatures, and persist in works because God watches wherever people are.
TUSTARI:82:6/r7.anchor: ألزموا قلوبكم، نحن مخلوقون وخالقنا معنا، ولا تملوا من أعمالكم، فإن الله شاهدكم حيثما كنتم

TUSTARI:82:6/r8.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r8.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r8.claim: Bring one's needs to God and remain at His door.
TUSTARI:82:6/r8.anchor: وأنزلوا به حاجاتكم، وموتوا على بابه،

TUSTARI:82:6/r9.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r9.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r9.claim: Recognize one's ignorance, weakness, and incapacity while relying on God as the knower, strengthener, and able one.
TUSTARI:82:6/r9.anchor: وقولوا: نحن جهال وعالمنا معنا، ونحن ضعفاء ومقوينا معنا، ونحن عاجزون وقادرنا معنا،

TUSTARI:82:6/r10.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r10.speaker: author
TUSTARI:82:6/r10.claim: Whoever remains in this reliance finds air, open space, earth, and sky all equal.
TUSTARI:82:6/r10.anchor: فإن من لزمها كان الهواء والفضاء والأرض والسماء عنده سواء

TUSTARI:82:6/r11.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:82:6/r11.speaker: عمر بن واصل
TUSTARI:82:6/r11.claim: Sahl's disciple Umar ibn Wasil said that ignorance in leaving God's protection was what deluded him when he recited the verse.
TUSTARI:82:6/r11.anchor: وقال عمر بن واصل تلميذ سهل: إذا قرأ هذه الآية قال: غرني الجهل بترك العصمة منك

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227#3/r1.speaker: عكرمة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227#3/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that this verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p227#3/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عكرمة في قوله ﴿ يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك ﴾ الآية قال أنزلت في أبي بن خلف

DAMGHANI:v1p49/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r10.claim: In the address asking what deceived a person about the generous Lord, al-insān refers to Usayd ibn Khalaf.
DAMGHANI:v1p49/r10.anchor: الإنسان أسيد بن خلف . قوله تعالى في سورة الانفطار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r11.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r11.claim: The human asked what deceived him about his generous Lord is identified as Kilda ibn Asīd, also called Asīd ibn Kilda.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p178/r11.anchor: والرابع عشر : كلدة بن أسيد ، وقيل أسيد بن كلدة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r4.claim: A third sense is forgiving or generous, as in the references to the gracious Lord.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p521/r4.anchor: والثالث : الصفوح : ومنه قوله تعالى في النمل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r3.claim: Karīm can mean forgiving, a quality associated with nobility and excellence.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p269/r3.anchor: والكريم: الصفوح، وذلك من الشرف والفضل، قال الله عز وجل: فإن ربي غني كريم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.claim: A singular form may address a collective; the author cites 'O human' and 'you are striving' alongside the statement about harm touching a person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p167/r7.anchor: وحد وهو يريد الجمع، كما قال: يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم (6)

NAHHAS:v5p167/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p167/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p167/r12.claim: ما is a complete noun in the nominative as the subject, while the second-person suffix is the object of غرّ.
NAHHAS:v5p167/r12.anchor: ما في موضع رفع بالابتداء وهو اسم تام والكاف في موضع نصب بغر

SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r1.claim: The common reading has triliteral غرك, with interrogative ما in the nominative as subject.
SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r1.anchor: العامة على " غرك " ثلاثيا و " ما " استفهامية في محل رفع بالابتداء

SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r2.speaker: ابن جبير والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr and al-Amash read ما أغرك; ما may be interrogative or exclamatory, and أغره means to lead someone into deception or make him deceived.
SAMIN-DURR:82:6/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن جبير والأعمش " ما أغرك " فاحتمل أن تكون استفهامية، وأن تكون تعجبية. ومعنى أغره: أدخله في الغرة أو جعله غارا

ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r7.claim: Gharra means to deceive and entice someone until they neglect what is due to God.
ZAJJAJ:v5p295/r7.anchor: أي ما خدعك وسول لك حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك

ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n3/r1.claim: Asad reads the question as warning that no one is wholly immune to fitnah; he compares 8:25 and says the answer comes in 82:9.
ASAD-NOTES:82:6#n3/r1.anchor: no human being is ever entirely immune against "that temptation to evil (fitnah)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p128/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p128/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p128/r2.claim: He connects this warning to 82:6, which asks what deceived a person about the Beneficent Lord.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p128/r2.anchor: In Sūrah Infiṭār, the words used to convey this very meaning are

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r1.claim: A report from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr gives the phrase with a lengthened ما, as an exclamation.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r1.anchor: روى عن سعيد بن جبير: "يا أيها الأنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم1"، ممدودة، على التعجب

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jinnī analyzes the analogy to “How patient they are over the Fire!” as involving two successive omitted genitives, like “a handful from the Messenger’s trace.”
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r2.anchor: ففيه حذف مضافين شيئا على شيء كما قدمنا في قوله: {فقبضت قبضة من أثر الرسول

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r4.claim: By analogy, Ibn Jinnī allows the verse to ask what prompted a person to be deluded by the Generous Lord.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r4.anchor: فكذلك يجوز أن يكون قوله أيضا: "ما أغرك بربك الكريم"، أي: ما الذي دعاك إلى الاغترار به؟

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jinnī glosses غر الرجل، فهو غار as “the man was heedless.”
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v2p353#2/r5.anchor: غر الرجل، فهو غار، أي: غفل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r8.claim: The question asks what deceived someone into abandoning obligations and what made him feel secure from God's punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r8.anchor: ما خدعك وسول لك الباطل حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك. والمعنى: ماذا أمنك من

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r9.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r9.claim: Ata says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r9.anchor: قال عطاء: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r10.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r10.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say it was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Shariq, who struck the Prophet without immediate punishment; the verse asks what God's forbearance led him to assume despite disbelief.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r10.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: نزلت في الأسود بن شريق ضرب النبي فلم يعاقبه الله عز وجل فأنزل الله هذه الآية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r11.claim: Qatada says Satan, the enemy empowered over the person, deceived him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r11.anchor: قال قتادة: غره عدوه المسلط عليه يعني الشيطان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r12.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r12.claim: Muqatil says that God's pardon, when He did not punish the person the first time, deceived him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل: غره عفو الله حين لم يعاقبه في أول [مرة] (2)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r13.speaker: السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says God's gentleness toward him deceived him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r13.anchor: وقال السدي: غره رفق الله به.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r14.claim: Ibn Masud says every person will meet God alone on Resurrection Day, where God asks what deceived him, what he did with his knowledge, and how he answered the messengers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r14.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: ما منكم من

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r15.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r15.claim: Asked how he would answer God, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said God's lowered veils had deceived him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r15.anchor: وقيل للفضيل بن عياض: لو أقامك الله يوم القيامة فقال: ما غرك بربك الكريم؟

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r16.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r16.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r16.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh says he would answer that God's past and present kindness had deceived him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r16.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ: لو أقامني بين يديه فقال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r17.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r17.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r17.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says he would answer that the generosity of the Generous One had deceived him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p352#2/r17.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: لو قال لي: ما غرك

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r10.claim: The question asks what deceived and emboldened a person to disobey; calling God generous is meant to deter presumption, since generosity does not require neglecting wrongdoers or equating obedient and disobedient people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r10.anchor: أي شيء خدعك وجرأك على عصيانه

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r11.claim: The wording exposes Satan's false reassurance that one may do as one pleases because a generous Lord neither punishes nor hastens punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r11.anchor: فإنه يقول له افعل ما شئت فربك كريم لا يعذب أحدا

BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r12.claim: God's great generosity calls for earnest obedience, not immersion in sin under the illusion that grace makes it safe.
BAYDAWI-FULL:82:1-6/r12.anchor: كثرة كرمه تستدعي الجد في طاعته لا الانهماك في عصيانه اغترارا بكرمه

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r4.claim: Umar says ignorance is what deluded the human being.
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r4.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وابن أبي حاتم وابن المنذر عن عمر بن الخطاب أنه قرأ هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r5.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r5.claim: Ikrima identifies the human addressed as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن عكرمة {يا أيها الإنسان ما غرك} قال: أبي بن خلف

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r6.speaker: صالح بن مسمار
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r6.claim: Salih ibn Mismar reports that the Prophet recited the verse and answered its question with “his ignorance.”
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r6.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن صالح بن مسمار قال: بلغني أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v8p438/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r7.speaker: ربيع بن خثيم
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r7.claim: Rabi ibn Khaytham glosses what deluded him as ignorance.
DURR-FULL:v8p438/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن ربيع بن خيثم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r12.claim: God reproaches humanity: what warrants disobedience, association, and disbelief when He created them from nothing?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r12.anchor: ثم خاطب تعالى جنس ابن آدم على جهة التوبيخ والتنبيه على أي شيء أوجب أن يغتر بربه الكريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r13.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r13.claim: A report says the Prophet answered human ignorance deceived him; Umar also said this, citing 33:72.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r13.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ: «جهله» وقاله عمر وقرأ إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r14.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r14.claim: Qatada says the deceiver is the human’s enemy empowered over him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r15.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r15.claim: Some scholars say God’s concealment of sins deceived him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r15.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: غره ستر الله عليه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r16.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p446#2/r16.claim: Another says God’s generosity deceived him.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r1.claim: الكريم suggests His generosity deceived the person; this is kindness toward sinful believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r1.anchor: الكريم تلقن هذا الجواب، فهذا من لطف الله تعالى لعباده العصاة من المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r2.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r2.claim: Ibn Jubayr and al-Aʿmash read ما أغرك, meaning what called you to be deceived.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p447/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن جبير والأعمش: «ما أغرك» على وزن أفعلك، والمعنى ما دعاك إلى الاغترار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r10.claim: This is a threat asking what emboldened a person to disobey the great Lord and treat Him with unworthy deeds; it is not a cue to answer that God's generosity deceived him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r10.anchor: بل المعنى في هذه الآية: ما غرك يا ابن آدم بربك الكريم-أي: العظيم-حتى أقدمت على معصيته،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r11.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r11.claim: A hadith depicts God asking Adam's child on Judgment Day what deceived him and what answer he gave the messengers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r11.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث: "يقول الله يوم القيامة: ابن (1) آدم، ما غرك بي؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r12.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r12.claim: When a man recited the verse, Umar answered that ignorance was what deceived him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r12.anchor: أن عمر سمع رجلا يقرأ: {ياأيها الإنسان ما غرك بربك الكريم} فقال عمر: الجهل (2) .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r13.claim: Ibn Umar said, by God, that the person's ignorance deceived him.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r14.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع بن خثيم والحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Rabi ibn Khuthaym, and al-Hasan are also reported to have given the answer that ignorance deceived the person.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r14.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، والربيع بن خثيم (3) والحسن، مثل ذلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r15.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r15.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r15.claim: Qatada says no one deceived Adam's child except the enemy Satan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r15.anchor: وقال قتادة: {ما غرك بربك الكريم} شيء، ما غر ابن آدم غير هذا العدو الشيطان.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r16.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r16.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r16.claim: Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad imagines answering that God's lowered veils deceived him if asked what deceived him about God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r16.anchor: وقال الفضيل بن عياض: لو قال لي:"ما غرك بي (4) لقلت: ستورك المرخاة.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r17.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r17.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r17.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq imagines replying that the generosity of the Generous deceived him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r17.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: لو قال لي: {ما غرك بربك الكريم} لقلت: غرني كرم الكريم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r18.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r18.speaker: البغوي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r18.claim: Al-Baghawi cites some ishari interpreters who say naming God al-Karim cues the answer that His generosity deceived the sinner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r18.anchor: قال البغوي: وقال بعض أهل الإشارة: إنما قال: {بربك الكريم} دون سائر أسمائه وصفاته، كأنه لقنه الإجابة (5) .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r19.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r19.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r19.claim: Ibn Kathir rejects that inference as weak: God says al-Karim to remind people that they should not answer generosity with ugly acts and evil deeds.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p341#2/r19.anchor: لينبه (6) على أنه لا ينبغي أن يقابل الكريم بالأفعال القبيحة، وأعمال السوء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r1.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say the verse was revealed about al-Aswad ibn Shariq, who struck the Prophet without being punished at the time.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p342/r1.anchor: حكى البغوي، عن الكلبي ومقاتل أنهما قالا نزلت هذه الآية في الأسود بن شريق، ضرب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v10p7309/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r12.claim: Ghurūr is a delusive matter that makes someone ignorantly imagine safety from what should be feared.
JISHUMI:v10p7309/r12.anchor: الغرور: ظفور أمر يتوهم به جهلا الأمان من المحذور، غره يغر غرورا، واغتر به يغتر اغترارا.

MUQATIL:82:6-13/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r1.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abū al-Ashaddayn, named Asīd ibn Kilda, a one-eyed man of great strength. He boasted that if he held the handle of Paradise’s gate, many people would enter; he was killed at the conquest of Mecca.
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبى الأشدين، أسمه أسيد بن كلدة، وكان أعور شديد البطش

MUQATIL:82:6-13/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:82:6-13/r2.claim: Satan is what deluded the human being.

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r1.claim: The address is directed to those who deny resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { يأيها الإنسان } خاطب بهذا منكري البعث

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the human addressed as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الإنسان هنا: الوليد بن المغيرة

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r3.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r3.claim: Ikrima identifies the human as Ubayy ibn Khalaf.

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about Abu al-Ashadd ibn Kalda al-Jumahi.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r4.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في أبي الأشد بن كلدة الجمحي. عن ابن عباس أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r5.claim: The question means: what led you to disbelieve in your Lord, the Generous, who overlooks your sins?
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r5.anchor: « ما غرك بربك الكريم » أي ما الذي غرك حتى كفرت؟ «بربك الكريم» أي المتجاوز عنك

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r6.claim: Qatada says the devil assigned to the person deceived him.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r6.anchor: قال قتادة: غره شيطانه المسلط عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r7.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says his wicked devil deceived him.

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r8.speaker: الحسن عن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r8.claim: A report from al-Hasan, from Umar, says that foolishness and ignorance deceived him.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r8.anchor: وقيل: حمقه وجهله. رواه الحسن عن عمر رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r9.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r9.claim: Ghalib al-Hanafi reports that when the Prophet recited the verse, he said that ignorance had deceived the person.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r9.anchor: لما قرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r10.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r10.claim: Salih ibn Mismar says it reached them that the Prophet recited the verse and said ignorance had deceived the person.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r10.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r11.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r11.claim: Umar links the explanation to God's description of the human as unjust and ignorant.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r11.anchor: وقال عمر رضي الله عنه: كما قال الله تعالى إنه كان ظلوما جهولا

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r12.claim: Another explanation is that God's forbearance deceived the sinner because He did not punish him the first time.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r12.anchor: وقيل: غره عفو الله، إذ لم يعاقبه في أول مرة

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r13.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r13.claim: Asked what he would answer if God asked him this on Judgment Day, al-Fudayl ibn Iyad says God's lowered veils of concealment deceived him, since generous can mean one who conceals.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r13.anchor: قيل للفضيل ابن عياض: لو أقامك الله تعالى يوم القيامة بين يديه

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r14.speaker: ابن السماك
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r14.claim: Ibn al-Sammak's poem warns the sinner that God's reprieve and long concealment are what deceived him.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r14.anchor: نظمه ابن السماك فقال: يا كاتم الذنب أما تستحي والله في الخلوة ثانيكا غرك من ربك إمهاله

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r15.speaker: ذو النون المصري
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r15.claim: Dhu al-Nun al-Misri says many people are deceived while living under concealment without realizing it.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r15.anchor: وقال ذو النون المصري: كم من مغرور تحت الستر وهو لا يشعر

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r16.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر الأبهري
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r16.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir al-Abhari's poem addresses the arrogant: God granted respite, but the person confronted Him with sins without fearing their consequence.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r16.anchor: وأنشد أبو بكر بن طاهر الأبهري: يا من غلا في العجب والتيه وغره طول تماديه أملى لك الله فبارزته

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r17.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r17.claim: Ali called his servant repeatedly; when the servant explained that he trusted Ali's forbearance and felt safe from punishment, Ali approved the answer and freed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r17.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه صاح بغلام له مرات

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r18.claim: Some explain the question as asking what tricked and enticed the person into neglecting the duty owed to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r18.anchor: وناس يقولون: ما غرك: ما خدعك وسول لك، حتى أضعت ما وجب عليك

QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r19.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r19.claim: Ibn Masud says every person will meet God alone on Judgment Day and be asked what deceived him, what he did with what he knew, and how he answered the messengers.
QURTUBI-FULL:82:6-7/r19.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: ما منكم من أحد إلا وسيخلو الله به يوم القيامة، فيقول له: يا بن آدم ماذا غرك بي؟ يا بن آدم ماذا عملت فيما علمت؟
